svg.title: Mapping a reported symptom to the layer most likely at fault
svg.desc: Six hand-drawn rows, each pairing a complaint a user might make with the context layer to inspect first and what to look for there. Ignoring an instruction it followed yesterday points at layer 01, the system prompt. Calling the wrong tool points at layer 02. Forgetting a preference points at layer 03, memory. Being confidently wrong on a documented fact points at layer 04, retrieval. Losing the thread in a long chat points at layer 05, history. Answering a different question than the one asked points at layer 06, the user instruction being buried rather than placed last. A caption notes that some bugs span layers and that the layers should be walked in order.
svg.text: Which layer is at fault?
Users report a symptom in the language of layer 06. It almost always names a different layer.
Symptom the user reports
Layer to inspect
Look at
"It ignored an instruction it followed yesterday."
System prompt
A rule was edited, truncated, or buried.
"It calls the wrong tool, or invents parameters."
Tools / MCP
Vague names; too many tools competing.
"It forgot a preference I set earlier."
Memory & state
Nothing persisted, or never replayed.
"It is confidently wrong on a fact in our docs."
RAG / retrieved chunks
Never retrieved, or reranked out.
"It loses the thread in long chats."
Conversation history
Window overflow, or lost from the summary.
"It answers a different question than I asked."
User instruction
The request is buried, not placed last.
Some bugs span layers. Walk them in order and ask: is this layer carrying what it should, and nothing it should not?
